Producing an increasing sequence of finite-dimensional subspaces whose union is F-dense requires a countable F-dense subset of Lip(X), i.e. separability of F. All subsequent steps (the residual tests h_{n2}, Dini's theorem, the SCI bounds) are built on this dictionary.

issues.failure_explanation: If supp(omega) is a proper subset of X, the L^1(omega)-norm is not a norm on a general finite-dimensional W (nonzero functions vanishing on supp(omega) have zero L^1-norm), so 'all norms on W are equivalent' fails and the L^1-unit sphere S is unbounded, hence non-compact, in (W,sup-norm). Concrete counterexample: X=[0,1], omega=delta_0, W=span{1,x}, dyadic partitions with the node of the cell containing 0 equal to its right endpoint 2^{-n}. Then S contains {1+bx : b in R} (||1+bx||_{L^1}=1), while Q_n(|1+bx|)=|1+b*2^{-n}|, so the displayed supremum is infinite for every n; the lemma's conclusion fails. The lemma is the paper's justification that axiom (F2) holds for F = L^1, so the L^1 instantiation of the meta-theorem (and the abstract's 'uniform finite-dimensional quadrature compatibility' claim) is unproven in the stated generality.

issues.failure_explanation: The greedy selection is myopic: choosing * whenever it is currently admissible need not be extendable, so u_m(S) can die (bot) even when S contains a Silver tree with unboundedly many free coordinates. Counterexample: A = odd integers, x = (1,1,1,...), S := S_{A,x} union {(0,0),(1,0)}. S is a tree containing the Silver tree S_{A,x}, so S is in V. But the greedy gives u_1 = (*); u_2 = (*,*) because Sigma((*,*)) = 2^2 is contained in S cap 2^2 (the two added nodes fill the missing half); and u_3 = bot, because each of (*,*,*), (*,*,0), (*,*,1) has Sigma containing a level-3 node with second coordinate 0, none of which lies in S. Hence k_m(S)=0 for all m>=3; since every Y_m-block permutation then has order dividing 4, the uniform resolvent bound gives sigma_ap(K_{Psi(S)}) contained in {1,-1,i,-i}, so the non-torsion z_0 is NOT in sigma_ap(K_{Psi(S)}) although S is in V. The claimed inequality k_m(S) >= |m\A| already fails at m=3 (0 < 2). The inference 'chooses * whenever admissible, hence at least as many *-coordinates as any admissible witness' confuses local admissibility with extendability. Note also that the correct set {S : z_0 in sigma_ap(K_{F_S})} equals {S : sup_m k_m(S) = infinity}, a Borel set strictly contained in V (the counterexample lies in V minus this set), so the Borelness contradiction used to prove SCI_G = infinity cannot be derived from this family at all.

issues.failure_explanation: For a countable partition, the argument only yields sigma_inf(K|_{X_{j(n)}} - lambda) -> 0 along varying blocks j(n). This does not imply dist(lambda, union_j sigma_ap(K|_{X_j})) = 0: for general bounded operators a small lower norm does not force closeness to the approximate point spectrum (the epsilon-pseudospectrum can be much larger than the epsilon-neighborhood of sigma_ap), and the proof provides no mechanism (e.g. a uniform bound dist(lambda,sigma_ap(K|_{X_j})) <= h(sigma_inf(K|_{X_j}-lambda)) with h(t)->0) transferring residual smallness along varying blocks into membership in the closure of the union. The step is presented as definitional ('exactly means') but is a substantive unproven claim. For finite partitions it is trivially repairable (pigeonhole on j(n)), but the applications to the countable partition X = {x_infinity} sqcup sqcup_m Y_m (lem:sap-FS-formula, lem:spectrum_FS) genuinely need it; those applications also use the null block {x_infinity} of omega-measure zero, violating the lemma's hypothesis 0 < omega(X_j) < infinity (a degenerate-case slip that is separately trivial to repair).
